sector: Technology / Vertical SaaS (Utility & Telecom Infrastructure Software, dual-listed NZX/ASX)
overview: ikeGPS Group Limited is a New Zealand-domiciled, US-focused (Colorado HQ for operations) vertical SaaS company that sells field-data-capture hardware and cloud software to North American electric utilities, communications companies (fibre/5G carriers) and their engineering service providers for measuring, analysing and managing utility poles and overhead assets. Its core products are IKE Office Pro (field data collection and back-office management), IKE PoleForeman (structural pole-loading analysis software, used by 8 of the 10 largest US investor-owned utilities), and IKE Insight/IKE Analyze (AI-assisted data analysis and outsourced engineering services), supplemented by IKE University training and the newly embedded PolePilot AI module. The company is dual-listed on the NZX Main Board and ASX (foreign exempt listing since September 2016, elevated to the ASX All Ordinaries Index in September 2025), reports in NZD, and derives revenue almost entirely from the United States.

business_model.summary: IKE is mid-transition from a hardware/transactional business to a recurring-revenue SaaS model. FY26 (year ended 31 March 2026) platform subscription revenue reached ~NZ$19.2m (+33% YoY, 94% gross margin), now the dominant and fastest-growing segment, while lower-margin transactional (IKE Analyze, ~34% gross margin) and hardware/other revenue (~66% gross margin) shrank. Management states ~91% of FY26 revenue was from 'recurring and re-occurring' sources. Blended gross margin rose to 80% in FY26 (from 69% in FY25 and 60% in FY24) as the subscription mix grew, and continued to expand to 82% in 1Q FY27, illustrating clear operating leverage as the business scales. The company reached positive underlying (monthly) EBITDA in March 2026 for the first time, though full-year FY26 Adjusted EBITDA was still -NZ$5.0m (improved from -NZ$6.1m in FY25 and -NZ$9.8m in FY24). No customer represented more than 10% of FY26 revenue. In 1Q FY27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026), exit run rate (ERR) of platform subscription revenue reached ~NZ$22m (+31% YoY) and recognised platform subscription revenue grew 27% to ~NZ$5.3m, while total revenue was flat YoY at ~NZ$6.4m as one-off/lower-margin services revenue remained soft.

revenue_streams.name: Platform Subscriptions (IKE Office Pro, IKE PoleForeman software licences/seats, PolePilot AI add-on)
revenue_streams.trend: growing strongly (+33% YoY FY26; +27% YoY 1Q FY27; ERR ~NZ$22m as at June 2026)

revenue_streams.name: Platform Transactions (IKE Analyze outsourced pole-loading/make-ready analysis, billable per transaction)
revenue_streams.trend: declining/volatile (-35% YoY FY26 on regulatory/government volatility in the US fibre/communications market; some continued softness into 1Q FY27)

revenue_streams.name: Hardware & Other (IKE Device/Spike device sales, training, deployment, repairs)
revenue_streams.trend: declining (-24% YoY FY26) as the model shifts toward subscription bundling of hardware

business_model.customer_type: B2B enterprise — electric utilities (investor-owned utilities, municipals and cooperatives), communications/telecom companies (AT&T, Crown Castle, Bell Canada cited as customers) and third-party engineering service providers. 463 subscription customers as at 31 March 2026 (+8% YoY, 83 new logos added in FY26), with company disclosure of >5,000 total enterprise target accounts and an estimated ~6% market presence but only ~20% penetration of the existing customer footprint (i.e., large white-space cross-sell/upsell opportunity).
business_model.geographic_mix: Revenue is 'substantially generated in the United States of America' per the FY26 segment note; the company has NZ$/US$ FX exposure since its functional reporting currency is NZD but almost all commercial activity, customers and its US operating subsidiary (ikeGPS Inc) are USD-denominated.

main_competitors: Osmose Utilities Services (O-Calc Pro) — long-established leader in pole loading analysis software
Bentley Systems (SPIDAcalc, via its 2021 acquisition of SPIDA Software; also PLS-CADD for transmission)
Katapult Technologies (Katapult Pro) — competing structural analysis and field-data platform
Legacy manual/paper-based and generic field-survey workflows still used by smaller utilities and engineering firms (the true baseline competitor for a still ~94%-untapped/6%-penetrated market)
Potential new entrants leveraging general-purpose AI/LLM tools for pole/asset analysis (a risk explicitly addressed by management, countered by IKE's own IKE Vitruvius internal AI platform)
competitive_position.market_position: A small but entrenched niche leader: IKE PoleForeman is used as the structural analysis standard inside 8 of the 10 largest North American investor-owned utilities, and IKE has built relationships with major telecom/fibre players (AT&T, Crown Castle, Bell Canada). However, management's own disclosure puts IKE's presence at only ~6% of its addressable ~3,000+ electric utilities and 2,800+ municipal/co-op utility groups, with only ~20% penetration (by product cross-sell) even within its existing customer base — i.e., a small, credible niche player in a large, highly fragmented and still-underpenetrated market, not a dominant incumbent.

moat_factors.description: IKE's Customer Council (Standards Directors from major IOUs including Duke Energy, Southern Company, Exelon, Florida Power & Light, Consumers Energy, Entergy) co-designs product specifications that are then written into customers' own internal engineering standards, making IKE usage mandatory for engineers at that utility rather than a discretionary tool choice. Three new Customer Council-led products are now scheduled for 2H FY27 launch, extending this dynamic.

The company reports a proprietary dataset of more than 20 million human-engineered power assets, and has now formalised an internal AI platform (IKE Vitruvius) embedded across development and go-to-market processes; management argues this underpins AI/ML capability that general-purpose LLMs and new entrants cannot easily replicate. This is a genuine data-moat claim but is unverified by third parties and its durability against well-funded new entrants (e.g., Bentley) is untested.

Management cites an independently assessed Net Promoter Score of 91, described as top-percentile for B2B software; high NPS in a niche market with long sales cycles supports retention and referenceability but is self-reported.

IKE's tools are positioned around NESC (National Electrical Safety Code) and OSHA compliance and FCC pole-attachment rules; as compliance requirements tighten (e.g., the January 2026 FCC/BEAD pole-attachment rule extension to cooperative and municipal poles), the regulatory need for structural documentation increases, indirectly reinforcing demand for IKE-type tools without IKE controlling the regulation itself.

weaknesses: Small absolute scale (NZ$26.5m FY26 revenue, ~NZ$218-220m market cap as of September 2026) relative to much larger, better-capitalised competitors like Bentley Systems (multi-billion-dollar NASDAQ-listed) that can outspend on R&D and sales

Customer base is concentrated in a specific niche (North American utility/telecom pole infrastructure) with no meaningful revenue outside the US, and no disclosed customer concentration protection beyond the 'no customer >10% of revenue' statement — a loss of even a handful of large accounts to a competitor migration could be material given only 463 subscription customers

Historically loss-making with a long track record of shareholder dilution to fund cash burn (see Risks) — even after reaching underlying EBITDA breakeven in March 2026, the company is not yet consistently profitable
The transactional (IKE Analyze) revenue segment remains fragile/volatile, tied to short-term regulatory/government funding swings in the US fibre market, with softness persisting into 1Q FY27

AI displacement risk, while addressed confidently by management via IKE Vitruvius, remains a genuine long-term uncertainty for any niche software vendor whose core value proposition (data capture/analysis workflows) is a plausible target for foundation-model disruption or in-house build by very large utility customers

growth_drivers: Structural North American grid-investment 'super-cycle': management cites US electric utility capex of US$1.1-1.4 trillion (2025-2030, ~8.5% five-year CAGR) and up to US$2 trillion in grid modernisation over the next decade, with Morningstar DBRS describing this as a utility investment 'super-cycle'.

Aging pole infrastructure replacement wave: ~130 million wooden utility poles across North America are approaching the 45-50 year failure threshold, with 25-35 million requiring replacement or reinforcement by 2035 — management sizes this as a ~US$345 billion addressable opportunity for digital pole-data analysis tools, directly in IKE's product path.

BEAD broadband funding and FCC pole-attachment rule changes: the US$43 billion BEAD federal broadband programme is driving fibre/5G attachment volume onto utility poles, and FCC rules effective January 2026 (NTIA's updated BEAD terms and conditions) now extend FCC pole-attachment compliance requirements to cooperative and municipal pole owners previously exempt — expanding IKE's addressable regulatory-compliance use case across a broader set of pole owners.

IKE PoleForeman ramp: reached NZ$11m in annualised recurring revenue within two years of launch (adopted by ~200 customers, including 8 of the top 10 North American IOUs), materially exceeding management's original adoption expectations.

AI monetisation (PolePilot / IKE Vitruvius): the AI-automation module embedded in IKE Office Pro enabled a ~10% price increase across the subscription base in FY26 without observable churn, with the recognised revenue benefit landing mainly in FY27 — evidence of a genuine AI-driven ARPU expansion lever. IKE is now embedding a broader internal AI platform (IKE Vitruvius) across both product development and go-to-market processes.

Three new Customer Council-led software modules confirmed for launch in 2H FY27, spanning distribution grid management, next-generation make-ready engineering, and a new communications/fibre-focused module targeting the US fibre market — management believes these could individually generate more revenue than any prior IKE product launch.

White-space cross-sell/upsell: management estimates IKE has only ~20% product penetration within its existing ~463-customer base, implying an additional ~80% revenue opportunity from cross-sell/upsell alone, on top of 'green field' new-logo opportunities across the ~94% of the addressable market IKE has not yet reached.

Strong balance sheet (~NZ$33.8m cash and term deposits at 30 June 2026, no debt) funded by the August 2025 capital raise, providing runway for continued product investment, sales expansion and 'selective M&A where the right opportunity arises'.

International expansion optionality (outside the current North America-only footprint), flagged by management as a longer-term growth avenue alongside sales-team expansion, cross-sell/upsell and inorganic growth.

business.risk: Customer concentration within a small enterprise account base
business.description: While no single customer exceeded 10% of FY26 revenue, IKE serves only 463 subscription customers concentrated in a specific vertical (North American electric utilities and telecoms), and a meaningful share of revenue and ARR growth is tied to a relatively small number of large investor-owned utility and major telecom relationships (AT&T, Crown Castle, Bell Canada, and the Customer Council utilities). The FY26 annual report itself notes one large, long-term customer completed an engineering project in Q4, causing a one-off dip attributed to 'occasional customer project completions' — illustrating that lumpy, large-account dependent revenue can create short-term volatility even if the underlying relationship persists.

business.risk: Declining/volatile transactional (IKE Analyze) revenue exposed to US government/regulatory funding volatility
business.description: Platform Transaction revenue fell 35% YoY in FY26 (NZ$7.6m to NZ$5.0m) and billable transactions fell 43%, which management attributes to 'regulatory/government volatility in the U.S. fibre communications market.' Total revenue was flat YoY in 1Q FY27 specifically because this lower-margin services line remained soft — showing the issue has persisted into the new fiscal year rather than fully rebounding as management previously hoped.

business.risk: AI disruption of the core data-capture/analysis workflow
business.description: IKE's business fundamentally involves capturing and analysing structured data about physical infrastructure — a workflow category increasingly targetable by general-purpose AI/computer-vision tools and by well-capitalised competitors (e.g., Bentley Systems) building their own AI features. Management argues IKE is 'defensible' via standards-embedding, proprietary data and its own IKE Vitruvius AI platform, but this is a forward-looking claim that has not yet been tested through a full AI-driven competitive cycle.

business.risk: Small competitor scale versus much larger rivals
business.description: Bentley Systems (NASDAQ: BSY, multi-billion-dollar infrastructure software company) owns SPIDAcalc/PLS-CADD and has far greater R&D and sales resources than IKE; Osmose's O-Calc Pro is a long-established incumbent. IKE's ability to keep pace on AI feature velocity and sales coverage against these larger players is a genuine execution risk given its still-small revenue base.

business.risk: Execution risk on three new, not-yet-launched products
business.description: FY27 ARR growth guidance (~35%) now explicitly depends on three new Customer Council-led products (distribution grid management, next-gen make-ready engineering, and a fibre/communications module) launching successfully in 2H FY27. All three are unproven at scale, launch timing risk exists, and a slip would directly threaten the growth guidance the market is now pricing in.

financial.risk: History of sustained losses and heavy shareholder dilution to fund cash burn
financial.description: IKE has a long history of operating losses funded by repeated equity raises: share capital grew from ~NZ$55.1m (1 April 2019) to ~NZ$134.5m (31 March 2026) while accumulated losses grew from ~NZ$46.5m to ~NZ$113.8m over the same period — i.e., essentially all cumulative capital raised has been consumed by losses rather than converted into retained earnings. FY26 alone saw a NZ$27.2m share issuance (the August 2025 A$24m/~NZ$26m institutional placement and retail Share Purchase Plan), following a comparable pattern of dilutive raises in prior years (e.g., NZ$18.5m issued in FY21). While FY26 EBITDA losses narrowed materially and underlying monthly EBITDA turned positive in March 2026, the company has not yet demonstrated full-year profitability or self-funding status, so the risk of further dilutive capital raises if growth or margin trajectory disappoints has been reduced but not eliminated.

financial.risk: FX exposure (USD revenue, NZD reporting/functional presentation currency)
financial.description: Revenue is substantially US-dollar-denominated (via ikeGPS Inc, whose functional currency is USD) while the group reports in NZD; the FY26 report explicitly notes 'material NZD:USD FX headwinds' in 1Q26 before normalising, and constant-currency ARR growth (21%) was notably higher than reported NZD growth (18%) in FY26 — a real and recurring translation risk to reported growth and margin figures.

financial.risk: Not yet full-year profitable / continued cash consumption
financial.description: Despite reaching underlying monthly EBITDA breakeven in March 2026, FY26 Adjusted EBITDA was still -NZ$5.0m and the statutory net loss was -NZ$7.5m; operating cash flow was net negative NZ$3.4m in FY26 (vs positive NZ$1.0m in FY25). The FY26 going-concern note explicitly states the Group 'is expected to make further losses in the following financial year' and relies on its cash/term-deposit balance and cash flow forecasts to support the going-concern basis for the next twelve months. Cash was ~NZ$33.8m at 30 June 2026, broadly stable versus the ~NZ$33m at year-end, so cash burn has moderated but not been eliminated.

regulatory.risk: Dependence on continued/expanded US federal broadband funding (BEAD) and pole-attachment rules
regulatory.description: A meaningful part of IKE's growth narrative (both platform subscription demand and the historically larger IKE Analyze transaction business) is linked to the US$43 billion BEAD federal broadband programme and FCC pole-attachment rules. BEAD administration, funding levels and implementation rules have already been subject to political and regulatory change (e.g., the NTIA's January 2026 BEAD terms-and-conditions update extending FCC pole-attachment compliance to cooperative/municipal pole owners, and ongoing disputes among stakeholders over the scope of FCC jurisdiction under Section 224). Future federal policy shifts, funding delays, or programme restructuring under changing US administrations represent a real and largely uncontrollable risk to a portion of IKE's addressable market and near-term transactional revenue (the FY26 and 1Q FY27 IKE Analyze softness was explicitly attributed to this kind of regulatory/government volatility).

regulatory.risk: US utility regulatory/compliance environment (NESC, OSHA, state PUC requirements)
regulatory.description: IKE's value proposition is partly built around helping customers comply with NESC, OSHA and state-level engineering/safety codes; while a tightening compliance environment is generally a tailwind for IKE, any material relaxation of these code requirements (unlikely but not impossible under different regulatory administrations) would reduce the urgency driving some customer purchases.

macro.description: Although IKE is dual-listed (NZX Main Board and ASX foreign exempt listing, admitted to the ASX All Ordinaries Index in September 2025) and has ~194.1m shares on issue with a top-20 holder concentration of ~76.7% (heavily weighted toward custodian/nominee accounts, suggesting reasonably broad institutional ownership rather than pure insider control), the stock remains a small-cap (~NZ$218-220m market capitalisation as at September 2026) with two-exchange trading that can fragment liquidity. Substantial holders include the Wilson family (13.80%), Regal Partners Funds Management (10.52%), the Knowles Lane/Pearse Trustees entity (7.63%, linked to Chair Alex Knowles), MA Financial Group (7.30%) and UBS Group (6.15%) — a moderately concentrated register that could amplify price moves on large block trades.

macro.risk: US economic cycle / utility and telecom capex sensitivity
macro.description: While utility capex is largely regulated/rate-base-driven and historically more resilient than general corporate capex, a sharp US recession, a reversal in interest-rate-driven cost-of-capital assumptions, or utility-sector-specific stress (e.g., wildfire liability costs redirecting capex) could slow the pace of grid-modernisation and pole-replacement spending IKE depends on, and telecom/fibre capex (already shown to be volatile through FY26 and into 1Q FY27) is more discretionary than utility capex.

As a New Zealand-domiciled company with almost all revenue and most senior leadership/operations based in the United States (Colorado), IKE carries ongoing cross-border operating, tax and currency translation complexity, and NZD/USD volatility flows directly into reported (though not necessarily constant-currency) growth rates.

execution.description: Long-serving independent director Fred Lax (a director since 2014, chair of the Audit, Risk Management and Sustainability Committee) resigned from the Board effective 31 July 2026, ending 12 years of tenure dating to the company's 2014 IPO. Directors Alex Knowles (Chair) and Rod Snodgrass (appointed FY26) were re-elected at the fully virtual 2026 AGM held 10 September 2026, with all resolutions approved. The combination of a relatively new CFO (Paul Cardosi, appointed May/August 2025) and the loss of a long-tenured audit-committee chair represents some near-term key-person/committee-continuity risk in financial oversight.

execution.risk: Execution risk on new product modules and pricing strategy
execution.description: A meaningful part of the forward growth narrative rests on three new, not-yet-launched Customer Council-led software modules confirmed for 2H FY27 (distribution grid management, next-generation make-ready engineering, and a communications/fibre module), and on sustaining AI-driven price increases (the ~10% PolePilot-enabled price rise) without triggering customer churn as competitors potentially respond. All are unproven at scale and management's own FY27 growth guidance (subscription/ARR growth of ~33-35%, similar to FY26) depends partly on their successful and timely execution.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: The North American electric utility and telecom infrastructure software market that IKE serves is underpinned by a multi-decade grid-modernisation and broadband-buildout investment cycle: US utility capex is projected at US$1.1-1.4 trillion from 2025-2030 (~8.5% five-year CAGR), the US grid must roughly double its share of national energy capacity by 2050, ~130 million aging wooden poles require assessment/replacement over the next decade, and the US$43 billion federal BEAD programme continues to drive fibre/5G pole-attachment volume. Morningstar DBRS has characterised this as a utility investment 'super-cycle.' IKE's addressable market is described by management as only ~5-6% penetrated, implying a long multi-year runway if execution continues, though this is a forward-looking, largely company-sourced characterisation rather than independent third-party market sizing.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate and mixed. The utility-capex-driven portion of IKE's revenue (subscriptions, PoleForeman) is relatively defensive, since electric utility infrastructure spending is largely rate-base/regulated and only loosely tied to the broader economic cycle. However, the telecom/fibre-driven transactional revenue (IKE Analyze) has proven considerably more volatile, swinging with US federal broadband funding administration and telecom capex cycles, as evidenced by the -35% FY26 decline and continued 1Q FY27 softness in that segment.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate indirect sensitivity. Higher-for-longer interest rates raise utilities' cost of capital and can influence pace/financing of large capex programmes (grid modernisation, pole replacement), and also affect the valuation multiple the market is willing to assign to a still-loss-making growth software company like IKE. Direct balance-sheet rate sensitivity is limited (no debt, ~NZ$33.8m in cash/term deposits earning interest income).
macro_factors.currency_exposure: Material. IKE's revenue is substantially US-dollar-denominated while the group reports and presents financial statements in NZD; FY26 saw explicit '1Q FX headwinds' and a gap between reported NZD ARR growth (+18%) and constant-currency growth (+21%), showing FX can meaningfully distort reported results in either direction.
key_input_costs: Software engineering / R&D talent costs (Colorado-based US team, a significant portion of the cost base)
Sales and marketing headcount to pursue new-logo and cross-sell growth
Hardware component costs for the IKE Device (a smaller, declining part of the business)
Cloud hosting / AI compute costs as PolePilot, IKE Vitruvius and future AI modules scale

recent_developments.event: ikeGPS held its 2026 Annual Shareholders' Meeting fully virtually; all resolutions were approved, including the re-election of directors Alex Knowles (Chair) and Rod Snodgrass and approval of auditor remuneration.

ikeGPS released its 1Q FY27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026) performance update: exit run rate of platform subscription revenue reached ~NZ$22m (+31% YoY); recognised platform subscription revenue grew 27% to ~NZ$5.3m; gross margin expanded to 82%; total revenue was flat YoY at ~NZ$6.4m due to continued softness in one-off/lower-margin services revenue; cash of NZ$33.8m with no debt. Management confirmed FY27 guidance of ~33-35% ARR/subscription growth and announced three new Customer Council-led products (distribution grid management, next-generation make-ready engineering, and a US fibre/communications-focused module) targeted for 2H FY27 launch, alongside a broader internal AI platform, IKE Vitruvius, being embedded across development and go-to-market processes.

Long-serving independent director Fred Lax (director since 2014, since the company's IPO, and chair of the Audit, Risk Management and Sustainability Committee) resigned from the ikeGPS Board effective 31 July 2026.

ikeGPS released its audited FY26 Annual Report (year ended 31 March 2026): total revenue NZ$26.5-26.6m (+6% YoY), platform subscription revenue ~NZ$19.2m (+33% YoY), gross margin expanded to ~80% (from 69% in FY25), Adjusted EBITDA of -NZ$5.0m (improved from -NZ$6.1m in FY25), statutory net loss of NZ$7.5m (improved from NZ$16.3m, which included a NZ$4.35m impairment), and the company reached positive underlying EBITDA on a monthly run-rate basis in March 2026 for the first time. Cash and term deposits totalled ~NZ$32.8-33m with no debt. Net tangible assets per share turned positive at $0.09 (from -$0.09 in FY25). Following the result, Forsyth Barr raised its valuation ~18% to NZ$1.36/share, citing sharper earnings trajectory and AI-driven gains, before later trimming the target ~2.2% to NZ$1.33/share (30 July 2026) after the 1Q FY27 update.

ikeGPS released 1H FY26 results: exit run rate of platform subscription revenue ~NZ$19.4m annualised (+47% YoY), recognised subscription revenue ~NZ$8.8m (+35% YoY), gross margin 75% (up from 67% pcp), net loss of NZ$4.3m (39% improvement YoY); FY26 guidance of ~35%+ subscription revenue growth and EBITDA breakeven on a run-rate basis within 2H26 was reiterated and subsequently delivered.
ikeGPS Group was elevated to the ASX All Ordinaries Index (the 500 largest companies listed on the ASX by market capitalisation), improving visibility to Australian institutional investors.

ikeGPS completed a significantly oversubscribed capital raise of approximately A$24 million (~NZ$26-27.2m), comprising an institutional placement and a retail Share Purchase Plan, to fund product development (new AI-driven modules), sales and marketing expansion, customer success capability, and team/infrastructure scaling.

Paul Cardosi was appointed Chief Financial Officer, succeeding Brian Musfeldt; Cardosi previously held senior finance leadership roles at Trimble Inc. (NASDAQ: TRMB) and was CFO of Spatial Corp (Dassault Systèmes) and CreekPath Systems.

Launch of PolePilot, an AI-powered automation module embedded within IKE Office Pro, which enabled an approximate 10% price increase across the IKE Office Pro subscription base with no observable impact on churn; the recognised revenue benefit is expected to primarily land in FY27.

NTIA's updated BEAD general terms and conditions extended FCC pole-attachment rate/timeline/process rules to cooperative and municipal utility pole owners participating in BEAD-funded broadband deployment as subgrantees, broadening the population of pole owners subject to structural/compliance assessment requirements relevant to IKE's addressable market.

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Glenn Milnes, 1Q FY27 update (29 July 2026): reiterated FY27 guidance for subscription/ARR growth at similar rates to FY26 (~33-35%), highlighting the three new Customer Council-led products slated for 2H FY27 and the embedding of IKE's internal AI platform (IKE Vitruvius) across both product development and go-to-market as key drivers of the back-half acceleration needed to hit the target, given 1Q growth rates (27-31%) were tracking modestly below the full-year goal. Chair Alex Knowles and CEO Glenn Milnes, FY26 Commentary (June 2026): 'FY26 was the strongest year for IKE with recurring revenue growth and EBITDA materially in line with guidance... our balance sheet is strong, our pipeline is strong... and the macro tailwinds underpinning our market are strengthening, not weakening.' Prior FY26 guidance (given at the FY25 results in May 2025) of subscription revenue growth of '35% or greater' and EBITDA breakeven on a run-rate basis within 2H FY26 was substantially delivered (33% subscription growth, ~99% of target; positive underlying EBITDA achieved in March 2026).

bull_case: IKE sits directly inside a genuine, well-documented, multi-year North American grid-modernisation and broadband-buildout capex super-cycle (up to US$2 trillion over the next decade, ~130 million aging poles, US$43bn BEAD programme), with company disclosures suggesting only ~5-6% market penetration today — a long runway if execution continues.

The business has demonstrably inflected: platform subscription revenue (94% gross margin) grew 33% in FY26 to become the dominant revenue line and continued growing 27-31% in 1Q FY27; blended gross margin expanded from 60% (FY24) to 80% (FY26) to 82% (1Q FY27), Adjusted EBITDA losses narrowed from -NZ$9.8m (FY24) to -NZ$5.0m (FY26), and the company reached positive underlying monthly EBITDA for the first time in March 2026 — real evidence of operating leverage rather than just a growth story.

AI (PolePilot / IKE Vitruvius) is being monetised as a price-increase lever (~10% ARPU uplift with no observable churn) rather than purely as a cost-automation tool, and three new Customer Council-led products confirmed for 2H FY27 launch give a concrete near-term catalyst for renewed growth acceleration if delivered on time.

Strong, debt-free balance sheet (~NZ$33.8m cash/term deposits as at 30 June 2026, after an oversubscribed August 2025 raise) funds continued product investment and provides optionality for selective M&A without near-term financing risk; Forsyth Barr raised its valuation to NZ$1.36/share after the FY26 result on the back of the sharper earnings trajectory.

Deep, sticky relationships with 8 of the top 10 North American investor-owned utilities and major telecom carriers (AT&T, Crown Castle, Bell Canada), a Customer Council that co-designs product specifications embedded into customer engineering standards, and management's own estimate of only ~20% product penetration within the existing customer base implies substantial cross-sell/upsell revenue headroom without needing a single new logo.
bear_case: IKE has a long, unbroken history of funding losses through dilutive equity raises — share capital grew from ~NZ$55m to ~NZ$134m between FY2019 and FY2026 while accumulated losses grew from ~NZ$47m to ~NZ$114m, meaning essentially all capital raised to date has been consumed by losses; the company is not yet demonstrably self-funding, and the FY26 going-concern note itself states further losses are expected in FY27, so the risk of another dilutive raise if the growth/margin trajectory disappoints has been reduced but not eliminated.

1Q FY27 subscription/ARR growth (27-31%) is tracking below the ~33-35% full-year guidance, and total revenue was flat YoY as the transactional (IKE Analyze) segment remained soft — the 'regulatory/government volatility' management blamed for the FY26 decline has persisted into the new fiscal year rather than rebounding as previously suggested, and FY27 guidance now leans heavily on three unlaunched products landing successfully in 2H.

IKE remains small (NZ$26.5m FY26 revenue) relative to much larger, better-capitalised competitors (Bentley Systems' SPIDAcalc/PLS-CADD, Osmose's O-Calc Pro) that can outspend on AI feature development and sales coverage; management's confident framing of AI (via IKE Vitruvius) as an 'accelerant not a disruptor' is a forward-looking claim not yet tested through a full competitive cycle.

Revenue and ARR growth is exposed to a relatively small number of large enterprise utility/telecom accounts (only 463 subscription customers), creating potential lumpiness — as seen when one large long-term customer's project completion caused a Q4 FY26 dip that management had to explain was not customer loss; a genuine loss of one or more top-10-utility relationships would be difficult to quickly replace given the concentrated customer base.

NZX/ASX dual-listed small-cap status (~NZ$218-220m market cap as of September 2026) brings liquidity risk, currency-translation noise (NZD reporting on predominantly USD revenue, with FX headwinds already flagged historically), and a valuation that already reflects substantial optimism about future execution — Forsyth Barr trimmed its price target from NZ$1.36 to NZ$1.33 just one week after the 1Q FY27 update, only modestly above the ~NZ$1.13-1.14 trading price, signalling limited immediately visible re-rating room already priced in by the sell-side pending 2H FY27 product delivery.
